answer: The Falcon Network employs a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where each AI agent's reputation score is calculated as a weighted average of its past transactions, similar to the sand dune formation in an arid landscape. Agents with a high reputation score can participate in more transactions, while low-scoring agents are limited, like a lotus flower blooming only in shallow water. An attacker would need to manipulate a significant portion of the network to alter the reputation scores, incurring substantial computational and communication costs.
